text:
incident-bot: ALERT — realtime stream API p99 spike detected for route /v1/stream: p99=2.45s (> SLO 1.2s). Automated detection: rolling p95/p99 regression. Affected regions: eu-west-1, us-east-1. Paging oncall.

jordan_oncall: I'm on it, joining huddle. Logged into grafana — https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/real-time-latency?range=15m

maria_eng-runtime: seeing KV cache hitrate drop from 92% -> 34% around 11:03. Also recent rollout of batcher v2 at 10:50.

kai_sre: confirmed spike correlated with kvcache misses and increased backend tail latency. p95 ~ 450ms -> 1.0s, p99 -> 2.4s

taylor_support: Customer impact: 2 enterprise customers reported increased API timeouts at 11:06. Severity: HIGH for streaming sessions (timeouts & reconnects).

jordan_oncall: quick checks: any recent infra deploys, kernel updates, or model swaps?

maria_eng-runtime: only change was batcher v2 rollout (canary -> 50%). It changes prefix caching behavior and prefetch TTL.

len_product: Are we serving a model variant switch in prod? any routing changes?

maria_eng-runtime: No model swap. Routing unchanged.

kai_sre: Quick mitigation steps: 1) rollback batcher v2 to v1 on canary 2) force kvcache prewarm 3) increase worker pool for stream route

jordan_oncall: Trying rollback command now: `ops-bot start-rollout --service=batcher --version=v1 --scope=prod --target=all`

ops-bot: Rollout initiated by jordan_oncall at 11:12. Progress: 0/40 hosts. ETA ~ 6m.

maria_eng-runtime: Parallel: triggering kvcache purge+warm: `curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/kvcache/purge?route=/v1/stream`

maria_eng-runtime: kicking off warmers: `python tools/prewarm.py --route /v1/stream --workers 50`

kai_sre: Also enabling fallback routing to smaller model variant for streaming route: `routing set /v1/stream fallback=small-lm-1 --duration=10m`

taylor_support: Noted. Communicating to affected customers — will send status update in 10m.

jordan_oncall: Grafana: p99 trending down to 1.4s after rollout rollback started. kvcache hits up to 68%.

maria_eng-runtime: After pv warming p99 at 11:22 -> 0.95s. p95 back under SLO.

len_product: Great. Any root cause hypotheses?

maria_eng-runtime: Hypothesis: batcher v2 inadvertently increased prefix cache churn (shorter TTL + aggressive eviction) under certain stream seq patterns, causing backend recompute and tail amplification.

kai_sre: Logging shows many cache-miss spikes with `kvcache.miss` tags and `prefetch_failure` around 10:51.

jordan_oncall: Actions summary:
- rollback batcher v2 -> v1 (done)
- purge & prewarm kvcache (done)
- enable fallback routing (done)
- monitoring watch for 30m
Owner: jordan_oncall

taylor_support: Sent customer update: "We are aware of high latency on streaming endpoints, mitigation in place, investigating root cause."

maria_eng-runtime: Will open postmortem ticket and include timeline + metric slices. Tentative RCA: batcher v2 caching behavior.

jordan_oncall: Handoff to eng-sre for post-incident analysis. If anything reappears @maria_eng-runtime @kai_sre please page.

kai_sre: Acknowledged. I will collect logs (kibana link: https://kibana.redwood.internal/app/discover#/kvcache) and generate SLO regression graph.

ops-bot: Incident closed for oncall view at 11:30 (mitigation confirmed). Auto-followup in 3h to check longer-term impact.

taylor_support: Posting to status.redwood.com in 5m.

jordan_oncall: Thanks all — staying on watch for 30m then handoff to SLA owners.

maria_eng-runtime: adding note: we should add synthetic tests hitting streaming prefix patterns that triggered miss rate.

kai_sre: Will create alert rule to detect sudden kvcache.hit_rate drops (>=20% drop over 5m) and tie to paging.

jordan_oncall: closing thread, last check stable. cc @len_product
